theory.intro: A composite figure is made by joining simple shapes together. Its perimeter is still the distance all the way around the **outside**, so any side that has not been labelled must be worked out before you add.
facts: Perimeter $=$ the sum of every side on the **outside** of the figure.
Missing sides come from the matching totals: the widths across the top and bottom are equal, and so are the heights on each side.
Internal dividing lines are **not** part of the perimeter.
**Push-out shortcut:** an L-shape or a staircase pushes out into a rectangle, so $P = 2 \times (\text{overall width} + \text{overall height})$.
The shortcut fails whenever the figure has a step that goes **inwards** (a notch): each notch adds twice its depth to the perimeter.
steps: Fill in every missing side length using the matching totals.
Add all the side lengths around the outside.
Write the answer with the correct unit.

development.solution_text:
The staircase pushes out to a rectangle $18\text{ cm}$ by $14\text{ cm}$.
$P=2\times(18+14)$
$=2\times32$
$=64\text{ cm}$

mastery.solution_text:
Working around the outside, the boundary is made of $12$ square sides.
$P=12\times9$
$=108\text{ cm}$
